Internal Bureaucratic Frictions
'1. Localism An agrioutural econony reliant on the hand-pestle
breeds deep clan ties. Branch meetings devolve into clan meetings. Hard
to build a "militant Bolshevik Party" when loyalty is strictly local.
2. Native vs. Settler Rift
Hundreds of years of deep-seated feuds between native inhabitants of the
plains and hill settlers. When White troops arrive, native peasants use
them to attack settlers, destroying class unity.
3. The Careerist Threat
During periods of success, opportunists flood the open Party recruitment.
When terror strikes, they immediately defect and inform on comrades.

Core Conclusion:
Mao's genius was not merely ideological; it was architectural. He
engineered a self-sustaining system designed to extract power from the
precise geopolitical and demographic realities of 1920s China.
